items.title: Federal government failed to hold Epstein accountable
items.feedTitle: Federal government failed to hold Epstein accountable, Republican committee says
items.summary: A Republican-led House Oversight Committee released a scathing report after a 15-month investigation, finding that federal authorities failed for decades to hold Jeffrey Epstein accountable. The report identifies systemic failures across multiple agencies in their handling of the case. This finding underscores accountability gaps in high-profile law enforcement matters and comes as attention to Epstein's associates continues.

items.title: House Republicans elect Jim Jordan as minority leader
items.feedTitle: House Republicans elect Jim Jordan to serve as minority leader next year
items.summary: House Republicans elected Ohio Congressman Jim Jordan as their new minority leader following midterm losses that cost the party control of the chamber. Jordan, who chairs the House Judiciary Committee, defeated Rep. Steve Scalise of Louisiana in a secret ballot. The GOP also elected John Thune as Senate Republican leader. Both decisions reflect the party's leadership transition as it enters a period in the minority.

items.title: U.S. inflation persists, driven by food, energy, housing
items.feedTitle: U.S. inflation report highlights strain of rising food, energy and housing costs
items.summary: October inflation data shows persistent price pressures, particularly in food, energy, and housing costs, with limited relief for struggling Americans. The inflation reading came in slightly above expectations and suggests the country is headed for an annual rate of about 4% this year. The data complicates prospects for near-term interest rate relief and underscores affordability challenges facing consumers heading into winter.

items.title: Democrats control states needed for popular vote compact
items.feedTitle: Farewell to the electoral college? Democrats now control enough states to elevate the popular vote
items.summary: Eighteen states run by Democrats have now joined an interstate compact to award their Electoral College votes to whichever presidential candidate wins the national popular vote, marking a significant shift in electoral power. This development comes after Democrats gained control of additional state governments in the midterms. The compact could reshape future presidential elections by potentially elevating the popular vote over the Electoral College.

items.title: Credit card debt reaches record high as Americans struggle
items.feedTitle: Credit card debt mounts amid Democrats' push to cap interest rates
items.summary: New Federal Reserve data shows Americans' credit card balances increased by $22 billion in the third quarter, a 1.7 percent rise, as households continue to grapple with high inflation and cost-of-living pressures. Credit card debt has hit record levels, reflecting both economic strain and reliance on borrowing to maintain spending. Some Democratic lawmakers are pushing to cap credit card interest rates in response.

stlouis.title: St. Louis County advances HQ lease, considers Page proposal
stlouis.feedTitle: Council advances lease for St. Louis County HQ but will also consider Page's proposal
stlouis.summary: St. Louis County Council advanced a lease agreement for the county headquarters while also agreeing to consider an alternative proposal from Page. The council's dual approach allows for comparison of options before a final decision is made. Details on the financial terms and timeline for implementation remain under review.

stlouis.title: St. Louis seeks to tax data centers already operating there
stlouis.feedTitle: St. Louis wants data centers to pay up. First it has to figure out which ones already do.
stlouis.summary: St. Louis is pursuing a strategy to impose taxes on data center operators, but first must determine which facilities are already operating and their tax status. The city is working to establish a system to identify and properly tax the data center industry. This effort reflects growing municipal interest in capturing revenue from the booming data center sector.

stlouis.title: Schmitt says St. Louis police grant protected from Democrats
stlouis.feedTitle: Schmitt says ‘front-loaded’ $68 million St. Louis police grant safe from Democrats
stlouis.summary: Missouri Attorney General Eric Schmitt stated that a $68 million federal grant for St. Louis law enforcement is 'front-loaded' and thus protected from Democratic efforts to reduce police funding. Schmitt's comments come amid ongoing national debates over law enforcement budgets. The grant represents a significant federal investment in St. Louis public safety.

items.title: Three Iran-backed suspects plotted attacks including RAF Fairford incident, US says
items.feedTitle: Three Iran-backed suspects plotted attacks including RAF Fairford incident, US says
items.summary: Summary unavailable for this update.

items.title: Thomas Markle, Meghan's father, jailed after removing monitor
items.feedTitle: Thomas Markle, Meghan’s father, jailed after cutting off ankle monitor, DoJ says
items.summary: Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Meghan Markle, was jailed after US authorities reported he cut off his electronic monitoring device while under house detention in Florida. Markle had been arrested for possession of child sexual abuse material. His removal of the ankle monitor violated the terms of his release and led to immediate re-arrest.

items.title: Spain holds state funeral for train crash victims
items.feedTitle: Spain holds state funeral for 69 victims of deadly train crash
items.summary: Spain's King and Queen attended a state funeral for 69 victims who died in a deadly train collision near Toledo two weeks earlier. The event brought together families of the deceased and national leaders to mourn the tragedy. Twenty-eight survivors remain hospitalized from the crash, which was among Spain's deadliest railway disasters in recent years.

items.title: British comedian Walliams accused of sexual misconduct
items.feedTitle: British comedian and children’s author David Walliams accused of sexual misconduct
items.summary: An investigation by ITV News and The Guardian revealed multiple accusations of sexual misconduct against British comedian and children's author David Walliams, including an allegation of sexual assault of a 15-year-old. Walliams has denied the claims, stating he is not a sexual predator. The investigation involved interviews with multiple accusers spanning several years.

items.title: Israel's new parliament sworn in, leaders compete to form government
items.feedTitle: Israel's new parliament sworn in as leaders compete to form government
items.summary: Israel's new Knesset was sworn in following recent elections, with opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot receiving the first opportunity to form a government and potentially oust Benjamin Netanyahu as prime minister. Netanyahu's main rival now has the mandate to attempt coalition-building. The political transition comes amid ongoing debates over Israel's military operations and governance priorities.

items.title: Three workers die at Tata's iPhone parts plant
items.feedTitle: Three workers die at Tata’s iPhone parts plant in India’s Tamil Nadu
items.summary: Three workers died at a Tata Electronics facility in Tamil Nadu that manufactures iPhone parts, with reports suggesting asphyxiation as a possible cause. The incident has raised concerns about workplace safety and conditions at the plant. Families of the deceased have begun receiving the bodies as investigations into the cause of death continue.

items.title: Sonia Gandhi's memoir revisits political inheritance and losses
items.feedTitle: 'They will kill you too': Sonia Gandhi's turbulent journey in Indian politics
items.summary: In her new memoir 'Belonging: A Journey of Love,' former Congress president Sonia Gandhi offers an intimate account of her family's political legacy, including reflections on personal tragedies and political rivalries. The book has sparked discussion about her recollections of political figures and her family's role in Indian politics. Gandhi's account provides rare insight into behind-the-scenes political dynamics.

items.title: India garment makers rethink reliance on US
items.feedTitle: India garment makers rethink reliance on US after tariff shock
items.summary: Indian garment manufacturers are reconsidering their business strategies and export dependency on the United States following proposed tariff increases by the Trump administration. The proposed tariffs represent a significant threat to India's textile and apparel sector. Companies are exploring diversification and alternative markets to mitigate trade risks.

items.title: India's air quality efforts need not slow economic growth
items.feedTitle: India’s efforts to clean its air need not slow its economic growth
items.summary: Analysis suggests that India can pursue air quality improvements without necessarily sacrificing economic growth rates. The Hindu argues that environmental compliance and economic development are not inherently in conflict. The discussion comes as northern India faces severe post-Diwali pollution challenges annually.

items.title: Andhra Pradesh clears AI, electronics, renewable energy policies
items.feedTitle: Andhra Pradesh Cabinet clears policy frameworks to attract investments in AI, electronics, renewable energy
items.summary: Andhra Pradesh's cabinet approved new policy frameworks to attract investments in artificial intelligence, electronics, and renewable energy sectors. The government also cleared a $31.4 billion green integrated AI data center project at Visakhapatnam. These policies represent the state's effort to position itself as a technology and clean energy hub.

immigration.title: IBM ends H-1B, green card sponsorship for most roles
immigration.feedTitle: IBM Ends H-1B Visa, Green Card Sponsorship For Majority Consulting Roles
immigration.summary: IBM announced it is ending H-1B visa and green card sponsorship for the majority of roles in IBM Consulting, its largest division, citing the Trump administration's crackdown on skilled foreign worker programs. The decision affects foreign workers currently employed or seeking positions in the consulting unit. IBM's move follows broader corporate responses to tightened immigration policies and suggests a trend among tech firms reassessing visa sponsorship commitments.

immigration.title: End of automatic work permit extension confirmed by USCIS
immigration.feedTitle: Removal of Automatic Extensions for Certain Employment Authorization Documents
immigration.summary: The Trump administration confirmed the end of automatic extension of work permits by up to 540 days, finalized and in effect. Workers must now renew their employment authorization documents (EADs) before expiration rather than relying on automatic extensions. USCIS has provided guidance on required renewal procedures for affected workers.

immigration.title: DHS proposes removing deference to prior visa determinations
immigration.feedTitle: Removing Deference to Prior USCIS Determinations of Eligibility
immigration.summary: The Department of Homeland Security has proposed removing 8 CFR 214.1(c)(5), which currently gives deference to prior USCIS approvals when adjudicating requests to extend visa petitions involving the same facts. The proposal, not yet final, would increase scrutiny on visa extension cases and could affect H-1B and other employment visa holders seeking renewals. This represents a significant procedural change potentially impacting existing visa holders.

items.title: US inflation rose 0.4% in October, exceeding expectations
items.feedTitle: US inflation rose 0.4% in October as price increases cooled and gas costs dipped
items.summary: October inflation rose 0.4% from September, slightly above expectations, though representing a cooldown in price increases as gas costs dipped. Food and housing costs remain elevated, creating ongoing affordability pressures for consumers. The data raised market concerns about the Federal Reserve's rate-hike trajectory heading into year-end.

items.title: Oil prices fall below $90 as Trump signals Iran war 'over
items.feedTitle: Oil prices fall to lowest since August as Trump says Iran war is ‘effectively over’
items.summary: Oil prices fell to their lowest level since late August, with Brent crude dropping below $90 per barrel, after President Trump said the war with Iran is 'effectively over' and signaled restraint on further military strikes. Stock markets climbed on relief from the geopolitical de-escalation. The price decline reflects reduced Middle East conflict risks and softening commodity demand concerns.

items.title: Chip stocks' losses near $5 trillion as Nvidia plunges
items.feedTitle: Chip stocks' slide nears $5 trillion as Nvidia hits most extreme selling level since 2019
items.summary: Semiconductor stocks have fallen sharply, with losses approaching $5 trillion in market value, as Nvidia extended its decline to its most extreme selling level since 2019. The chip sector selloff reflects concerns about CEO Jensen Huang's alleged affair with a Chinese national suspected of espionage, as well as broader AI valuation pressures. The sector decline has rippled across tech-dependent markets globally.

items.title: Anthropic targets $1.4 trillion valuation in IPO
items.feedTitle: Anthropic targets valuation of up to $1.4tn in stock market flotation
items.summary: Anthropic, the AI chatbot developer behind Claude, is seeking a valuation of up to $1.4 trillion in its imminent stock market flotation, down from earlier expectations of $2 trillion as investor sentiment on AI has cooled. The company set an IPO price range of $70 to $78 per share. The lower valuation reflects broader market caution about AI company valuations despite Anthropic's strong revenue growth.

items.title: Boeing cuts 5% of commercial plane workforce
items.feedTitle: Boeing to cut about 5% of its commercial plane workforce
items.summary: Boeing announced it will cut approximately 5% of its commercial airplane workforce through a combination of layoffs and attrition as it moderates the pace of ramping up jet production. The job cuts reflect the company's efforts to manage production capacity and address supply chain challenges. The move signals ongoing headwinds in the commercial aviation sector.

finance.note: Oil prices rebounded below $90/bbl as Trump signaled restraint on Iran strikes, easing geopolitical risk premiums, while US stock futures ticked higher in early trading. However, October inflation data came in hotter than expected at 0.4% month-over-month, fueling bets on larger Federal Reserve rate hikes in December and triggering a sharp bond selloff with yields climbing 19 months' worth in a single session. Semiconductor stocks extended their steepest losses since 2019 as Nvidia plunged over 5% amid CEO scandal; watch for corporate earnings guidance and Fed rate expectations this week.

cards.title: Sleep and inflammation linkage
cards.insight: Chronic sleep deprivation triggers inflammatory pathways in the body, correlating with elevated cortisol and immune dysregulation. Poor sleep quality amplifies metabolic stress and weakens immune defenses, making vulnerability to infection and chronic disease more likely.
cards.takeaway: Prioritize consistent sleep schedules (7–9 hours nightly) and limit screen time before bed to stabilize circadian rhythms and reduce systemic inflammation.

cards.title: Movement as mental health anchor
cards.insight: Moderate-intensity physical activity—even 30 minutes of brisk walking—activates endorphin and serotonin pathways, offering acute mood elevation and long-term anxiety/depression risk reduction comparable to some pharmacological interventions.
cards.takeaway: Schedule movement during stressful periods; even brief walking breaks during workdays measurably reduce cortisol and improve emotional regulation.

cards.title: Nutrition's role in cognitive decline
cards.insight: Ultra-processed food consumption is associated with accelerated cognitive aging and increased dementia risk due to oxidative stress and vascular inflammation in the brain. Micronutrient deficiency (B vitamins, omega-3s, magnesium) directly undermines neuroplasticity.
cards.takeaway: Emphasize whole foods—vegetables, fish, nuts, legumes—to maintain nutrient density and protect long-term brain health from metabolic and inflammatory damage.

cards.title: Social connection as longevity factor
cards.insight: Perceived social isolation is associated with mortality risk equivalent to smoking or obesity; conversely, strong social bonds buffer stress responses and lower cardiovascular disease markers independent of age or baseline health.
cards.takeaway: Regularly engage in in-person social activity, even brief interactions; community and family connection are measurable protective health factors, not luxuries.

ai.title: Anthropic sets IPO range at $1.4 trillion valuation
ai.feedTitle: Anthropic bankers prepare to increase IPO valuation to $1.5tn or more
ai.summary: Anthropic announced an IPO price range of $70 to $78 per share, implying a valuation of up to $1.4 trillion on a fully diluted basis. The company's strong sequential revenue growth of 47% and expanding user base support the valuation despite broader AI sector pullback. Each of the seven co-founders plans to sell shares worth approximately $250 million at the midpoint of the price range.

ai.title: OpenAI posts steep losses despite $10 billion revenue
ai.feedTitle: Exclusive | OpenAI Continues to Suffer Heavy Losses as Revenue Rises to $10 Billion
ai.summary: OpenAI reported third-quarter revenue soaring nearly 50% to $10 billion, marking a 'blockbuster quarter,' but the company continues to post steep losses. The massive revenue growth reflects strong adoption of ChatGPT and enterprise services, but operational costs and infrastructure investment exceed income. The financial picture highlights the capital-intensive nature of AI development.

ai.title: New York AI safety law enforcement begins for major firms
ai.feedTitle: OpenAI, Anthropic face new oversight as New York’s AI safety law takes effect
ai.summary: New York is preparing to enforce its sweeping AI safety law, requiring major developers like OpenAI and Anthropic to register with the state, disclose safety practices, and report critical incidents or face significant fines. The law represents one of the first comprehensive state-level AI regulations in the US. Companies must comply with disclosure and safety requirements or face penalties.

ai.title: Nvidia CEO Huang's alleged Chinese spy affair impacts policy
ai.feedTitle: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with alleged Chinese spy: a timeline
ai.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's alleged affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy may cost him influence on US AI policy, even if he retains his position at the company. The scandal has raised national security concerns about technology sector vulnerabilities to foreign intelligence. US lawmakers are pushing to curtail China's access to advanced AI chips in response.
